Honeycomb construction, tailored to the window

Cellular shades, also called honeycomb shades, use enclosed fabric pockets rather than a single flat sheet. They are an option for bedrooms, living areas, and offices where you want a fabric shade with an insulating construction. We help you compare the cell size, fabric, and control system.

Single-cell and double-cell

The number and size of the cells affect the fabric profile. Compare samples at your window so you can see how the cell sizes look. Energy performance depends on the shade, its fit, the window, and how you use it.

Light filtering or room darkening

Light-filtering fabrics soften daylight. Room-darkening options reduce light through the shade, but mounting and edge gaps still matter. Think about morning sun in a bedroom and nighttime privacy in a front-facing living room.

Top-down and lift options

Selected systems let you change coverage from the top as well as the bottom. Ask which configurations are available for your dimensions. For high windows or several shades used together, compare manual controls with compatible motorization.

A closer look

Cellular Shades in Fort Wayne, Indiana

Struggling with high energy bills and uncomfortable rooms? Cellular shades - also called honeycomb shades - are the most energy-efficient window treatment you can buy. Their unique honeycomb structure traps air inside, creating insulation that keeps heat out during Indiana summers and warmth in during brutal winters. They're not just window coverings, they're an investment that pays you back.

At Beautiful Blinds and Shades, we help homeowners throughout Fort Wayne and Allen County choose cellular shades that actually make a difference on their energy costs. Our free in-home consultation shows you the insulation difference between single-cell, double-cell, and different cell sizes.

Why cellular shades work

Serious energy efficiency. The honeycomb pockets trap air, creating a barrier between your window and room. This reduces heat transfer significantly - up to 40% energy savings on windows according to some studies. That's real money back in your pocket.

Temperature control you'll notice. Rooms stay cooler in summer without blasting AC. They stay warmer in winter without cranking heat. Homeowners in Auburn and Kendallville with older windows see dramatic improvements.

Light control options. From sheer that filters light gently to blackout that blocks 99%, cellular shades handle whatever you need. Same energy benefits, different opacity.

Cordless and top-down/bottom-up available. Raise from bottom, lower from top, or both. Great for privacy while keeping upper windows open for light. Completely cordless options are safest for families in New Haven and Leo-Cedarville with young kids.

Noise reduction. The air pockets don't just insulate against temperature - they dampen sound too. Helpful for busy streets or bedrooms near active areas.

Clean, contemporary look. When lowered, they're smooth and unobtrusive. When raised, they stack compactly. They don't demand attention like some treatments do.

Single-cell vs double-cell

The cell construction affects performance and cost.

Single-cell (⅜" or ½" cells) - One layer of honeycomb pockets. Good insulation, lower cost. Works well for most applications. Popular choice for homes in Bluffton and Warsaw where budget matters.

Double-cell (⅜" or ½" cells) - Two layers of honeycomb pockets. Maximum insulation. Better for extreme temperature windows or rooms that never feel comfortable. Worth the upgrade for problem windows in older homes throughout Columbia City and Grabill.

Cell size matters too. Larger cells (½") provide more insulation but are more visible. Smaller cells (⅜") offer a more refined look with slightly less insulation. We'll show you the difference during your consultation.

Light control options

Sheer cellular shades - Soft, filtered light. Daytime privacy while maintaining brightness. Not for bedrooms where you need darkness.

Light-filtering cellular shades - Most popular option. Reduces glare, provides good privacy, keeps rooms naturally lit. Perfect for living rooms and offices in Huntertown and Woodburn.

Room-darkening cellular shades - Significantly reduces light. Good for bedrooms and media rooms. Not complete blackout but close.

Blackout cellular shades - Block 99% of light when combined with side tracks. Essential for shift workers, nurseries in Monroeville and Harlan, or anyone who needs serious darkness for sleep.

Best rooms for cellular shades

Bedrooms. Insulation keeps rooms comfortable for sleeping. Blackout options create darkness. Energy savings happen 24/7.

Living rooms with temperature issues. South and west-facing windows that make rooms uncomfortable get immediate relief. The insulation makes a noticeable difference.

Sunrooms and additions. These spaces often have temperature extremes. Cellular shades moderate the swings. Popular in three-season rooms throughout Syracuse and Hoagland.

Any window with an energy problem. Drafty windows, rooms that never feel right, spaces where AC or heat struggles - cellular shades address the root issue.

Home offices. Comfortable temperature plus light-filtering options equal better work environment. Less glare on screens too.

Top-down/bottom-up operation

This feature makes cellular shades incredibly versatile.

Lower from the top - Natural light comes in up high while maintaining privacy below. Perfect for bathrooms, bedrooms at street level, or ground-floor windows throughout Fort Wayne neighborhoods.

Raise from bottom - Traditional operation that most people are used to.

Adjust both independently - Create a band of light at whatever height you want. Ultimate flexibility for changing needs throughout the day.

Not all cellular shades need this feature, but when privacy plus light matters, it's worth having.

Motorization and smart features

Battery-powered motors work beautifully with cellular shades.

Seasonal automation. Program shades to lower during hottest part of summer afternoons, protecting rooms from heat gain. Raise them on winter mornings to let warming sunlight in. Set it and forget it.

Multiple shades, one control. Have cellular shades throughout your home in Angola or Kendallville? Adjust them all from your phone without walking room to room.

Smart home integration. Works with Alexa, Google Home, Apple HomeKit. "Alexa, close bedroom shades" actually works.

Quieter operation. Battery motors are whisper-quiet. No mechanical noise, no cords hanging down.

What to know before choosing cellular shades

They're not the prettiest option. We're being honest - cellular shades excel at function over fashion. The honeycomb structure is visible. If aesthetics matter most, roman shades might be better.

Dusting the cells can be tricky. Use a vacuum with brush attachment or compressed air. The pockets can collect dust over time, especially in light colors.

Side gaps allow some light. Standard cellular shades have small gaps where they meet the window frame. For total blackout, you need side tracks (which we offer).

More expensive than roller shades. The energy savings justify the cost, but the upfront investment is higher. Quality insulation isn't cheap.

Stack height varies by cell size. Larger cells stack bulkier than smaller cells when raised. Plan for about 2-3 inches per foot of shade length.

How much can you really save?

Real numbers from real homeowners: Many report 10-25% reduction in heating and cooling costs for the rooms with cellular shades. The exact savings depend on:

  • Your current windows (older, drafty windows see bigger improvements)
  • Cell construction (double-cell saves more than single-cell)
  • How consistently you use them (lowered shades insulate, raised shades don't)
  • Climate extremes (harsh Indiana winters and hot summers create more savings opportunities)

Common questions

How much do cellular shades cost?More than basic roller shades, less than premium roman shades. Pricing depends on window size, single vs double-cell, opacity, and features. We provide transparent pricing during your consultation.

Will they really lower my energy bills?For most homeowners, yes. The savings depend on your windows, insulation, and usage. Older homes with drafty windows see the biggest impact. We've heard consistent feedback from customers in Huntertown and Leo-Cedarville about noticeable comfort improvements.

How do I clean them?Regular dusting or vacuuming with brush attachment prevents buildup. For deeper cleaning, use compressed air to blow dust out of cells. Avoid soaking them - the honeycomb structure doesn't dry easily.

Do they provide privacy?Light-filtering and room-darkening options provide daytime privacy. At night with interior lights on, shapes may be visible through light-filtering fabrics. Blackout provides complete privacy.

Are they safe for kids?Choose cordless lift to eliminate cord hazards. Top-down/bottom-up options and motorization are also cordless. Safe operation is built into most modern cellular shades.

Can I get them motorized?Yes. Battery-powered motors integrate seamlessly with cellular shades. Popular for hard-to-reach windows or when you want automated seasonal energy management.

What colors do they come in?Wide range of neutrals plus some bolder colors. White and off-white are most popular because they look clean from outside regardless of your interior decor.

How long do they last?Quality cellular shades with proper care last many years. The fabric may fade with intense sun exposure, but the honeycomb structure holds up well. The lifting mechanism should operate smoothly for a long time.

Are cellular shades the same as pleated shades?

They can look similar from the room, but cellular shades have enclosed pockets. Pleated shades use folded fabric without the same honeycomb structure. Compare how they are made and how much light each fabric lets through.

Will cellular shades lower my energy bill?

Cellular shades can help insulate a window. Any energy savings depend on the shade, its fit, your windows, the weather, and how you use it.

Can I have top-down/bottom-up and motorization?

Available combinations vary by product and size. Tell us the way you want to adjust the shade so we can check the exact configuration before preparing the order.
